Common.language.context: Accessible name of the language switcher, a row of four chips. The languages inside it wear their own untranslated names.

Common.loadingRoster.context: Status line while the list of students is still being read. Shown on the dashboard and the check-in screen.

Common.loadingHistory.context: Status line while past attendance is still being read. "History" here is the record of who came, not a browser history.

Common.loading.context: Generic in-progress line with a trailing ellipsis. Keep the ellipsis.

Common.loadingAria.context: Screen-reader-only version of the loading line. No ellipsis — a screen reader would read it aloud.

Common.required.context: Validation message under an empty form field that must be filled in. Not a label saying a field is required.

Common.cancel.context: Button that abandons whatever dialog is open, changing nothing. Never a button that cancels a gathering — that is EventDetail.yesCancel.

Common.remove.context: Button that takes one row out of a list being edited, e.g. a child from a quick-add form. Not a delete.

Common.delete.context: Button that destroys something permanently. Distinct from Common.remove, which takes a row out of a list being edited.

Common.grade.context: Field label for a school year. The values are Pre-K, K, then 1st–12th.

Common.noGrade.context: The option meaning this student has no school year on file. An answer, not a blank.

Common.lastName.context: Field label. Family name. In Chinese this is the surname, which comes first in a written name — the label still means the family name.

Common.close.context: Accessible name of the × that dismisses a modal.

Common.done.context: Button that closes a sheet the reader has finished with. Not a confirmation — nothing is saved by pressing it.

Common.reload.context: Button offered after Tally updated while the page was open. Reloads the browser page.

Common.clear.context: Key on the kiosk's drawn keyboard and phone pad: wipe what has been typed so far. A verb.

Common.dismiss.context: Accessible name of the × on a toast — the small message that slides in after an action.

Common.undo.context: Button that takes back the action just performed — a check-in, a release. Always reversible; never a delete.

Common.status.context: Field label for whether a person is active or inactive. Not a sync status, not an event status.

Common.active.context: Status value: this person is on the roster and appears at check-in.

Common.inactive.context: Status value: this person is kept in history but appears on no roster.

Common.search.context: Accessible name and placeholder for a search input.

Common.role.context: Field label for what a team member is allowed to do (counselor, core team, admin).

Common.theme.context: Accessible name of the light/dark appearance control. Visual theme, not a topic.

Common.birthday.context: Field label for a date of birth.

Common.profile.context: Card heading over a student's own details — name, grade, birthday. Not an account profile.

Common.attendance.context: Card heading over the list of gatherings a student came to.

Common.call.context: Button that dials a phone number. A verb.

Common.text.context: Button that opens a text message (SMS) to a phone number. A VERB, not the noun — some languages need "send a message".

Common.email.context: Button that opens an email to an address. A verb.

Common.later.context: Section heading on the events list, over gatherings further out than the next few. A time, not a "do this later" button.

Common.grades.context: Field label for a range of school years, e.g. which grades a gathering is for. Plural of Common.grade.

Common.gathering.context: Field label for which gathering a thing belongs to. The recurring meeting, not a one-off trip.

Common.unit.context: Field label beside a number in the custom-repeat editor: the number is "every N", this picks weeks, months or years.

Common.size.context: Field label in the name-tag designer: how big this line of text prints. Font size, not paper size.

Common.align.context: Field label in the name-tag designer: left, centre or right on the label.

Common.bold.context: Toggle in the name-tag designer: print this line in bold.

Common.copies.context: Field label in the name-tag designer: how many identical labels to print per child.

Nav.checkIn.context: Nav item. Opens the screen where a counselor marks who is here. A verb phrase.

Nav.insights.context: Nav item. Opens the dashboard of counts and trends. Pinned identical to Dashboard.title.

Nav.events.context: Nav item. Opens the calendar of gatherings and one-off trips. The umbrella term covering both.

Nav.review.context: Nav item. Opens the queue of families who registered themselves and are waiting for a person to approve them.

Nav.kiosk.context: Nav item. Opens the lobby self-service screen. Named for the tablet on the wall.

Nav.team.context: Nav item. Opens the list of counselors and admins. Pinned identical to Team.title.

Nav.settings.context: Nav item. Pinned identical to Settings.title.

Events.limitedTag.context: The whole of what an admin sees on a gathering somebody has fenced: a padlock and how many people are on it. Admin-only, and there are two or three per church, so it is a mark to learn rather than a sentence to read. The padlock-with-key is deliberately not the plain 🔒 the rest of the app uses for a gathering you cannot take — an admin passes this one. JobChip.queuedLong.context: One of nine states an edit can be in on its way to the church directory. This family is the legend the ~95 other sync strings defer to, so the nine must stay distinguishable from each other in translation — in particular the three that resolve themselves (queued, sending, waiting, stalled) must not collapse into the three that need a person (differs, failed, orphaned). Written down, not sent yet, and the only state a person can still cancel. *Long* is the row form and may be a phrase.

JobChip.queuedShort.context: Chip form of "queued": written down, not sent, still cancellable. *Short* must fit inside a chip a few characters wide.

JobChip.queuedTitle.source: Written down and not sent yet — you can still cancel it.
JobChip.queuedTitle.context: Tooltip explaining the queued chip. The cancellability is the point — it is the one state a person can still take back.

JobChip.sendingLong.context: One of nine states an edit can be in on its way to the church directory. This family is the legend the ~95 other sync strings defer to, so the nine must stay distinguishable from each other in translation — in particular the three that resolve themselves (queued, sending, waiting, stalled) must not collapse into the three that need a person (differs, failed, orphaned). The request is in the air right now. *Long* is the row form and may be a phrase.

JobChip.sendingShort.context: Chip form of "sending": in the air right now. *Short* must fit inside a chip a few characters wide.

JobChip.sendingTitle.source: Tally is sending this change now.
JobChip.sendingTitle.context: Tooltip on the sending chip. Says only that it is moving, not stuck.

JobChip.waitingLong.context: One of nine states an edit can be in on its way to the church directory. This family is the legend the ~95 other sync strings defer to, so the nine must stay distinguishable from each other in translation — in particular the three that resolve themselves (queued, sending, waiting, stalled) must not collapse into the three that need a person (differs, failed, orphaned). The directory asked Tally to slow down; it starts again by itself. Must NOT read the same as queued — a reader who confuses them tries to cancel something uncancellable. *Long* is the row form and may be a phrase.

JobChip.waitingShort.context: Chip form of "waiting": throttled, resumes by itself. *Short* must fit inside a chip a few characters wide.

JobChip.waitingTitle.source: Your church directory asked Tally to slow down. It resumes on its own — nothing is stuck.
JobChip.waitingTitle.context: Tooltip on the waiting chip. "Nothing is stuck" is the reassurance that stops somebody re-sending.

JobChip.landedLong.context: One of nine states an edit can be in on its way to the church directory. This family is the legend the ~95 other sync strings defer to, so the nine must stay distinguishable from each other in translation — in particular the three that resolve themselves (queued, sending, waiting, stalled) must not collapse into the three that need a person (differs, failed, orphaned). Done: the edit is in the church directory. *Long* is the row form and may be a phrase.

JobChip.landedShort.context: Chip form: done, the edit is in the directory. *Short* must fit inside a chip a few characters wide.

JobChip.differsLong.context: One of nine states an edit can be in on its way to the church directory. This family is the legend the ~95 other sync strings defer to, so the nine must stay distinguishable from each other in translation — in particular the three that resolve themselves (queued, sending, waiting, stalled) must not collapse into the three that need a person (differs, failed, orphaned). A conflict: somebody changed the same field on the other side, so the value now stored is one nobody typed. Needs a person — it will not resolve itself. *Long* is the row form and may be a phrase.

JobChip.differsShort.context: Chip form: a conflicting change on the other side. Needs a person. *Short* must fit inside a chip a few characters wide.

JobChip.differsTitle.source: This field was changed in your church directory. Review and resolve the difference.
JobChip.differsTitle.context: Tooltip on the conflict chip. "It will not resolve itself" is what separates this from waiting and stalled.

JobChip.mergedLong.context: One of nine states an edit can be in on its way to the church directory. This family is the legend the ~95 other sync strings defer to, so the nine must stay distinguishable from each other in translation — in particular the three that resolve themselves (queued, sending, waiting, stalled) must not collapse into the three that need a person (differs, failed, orphaned). The person being edited was merged into somebody else in the directory; the correction landed on the survivor under a different id. *Long* is the row form and may be a phrase.

JobChip.mergedShort.context: Chip form: the person was merged into another in the directory. *Short* must fit inside a chip a few characters wide.

JobChip.mergedTitle.source: The person you edited was merged into somebody else in your church directory. Your correction landed on them, under a different id.
JobChip.mergedTitle.context: Tooltip on the merged chip. The edit did land — on a different record than the one the reader picked.

JobChip.failedLong.context: One of nine states an edit can be in on its way to the church directory. This family is the legend the ~95 other sync strings defer to, so the nine must stay distinguishable from each other in translation — in particular the three that resolve themselves (queued, sending, waiting, stalled) must not collapse into the three that need a person (differs, failed, orphaned). The directory refused the edit outright. Needs a person. *Long* is the row form and may be a phrase.

JobChip.failedShort.context: Chip form: refused. *Short* must fit inside a chip a few characters wide.

JobChip.failedTitle.source: Your church directory refused this edit. Open it to see why.

JobChip.orphanedLong.context: One of nine states an edit can be in on its way to the church directory. The person this edit names no longer exists in the directory — deleted there. Needs a person. *Long* is the row form and may be a phrase.

JobChip.orphanedShort.context: Chip form: the person no longer exists in the directory. *Short* must fit inside a chip a few characters wide.

JobChip.orphanedTitle.source: The person this edit names no longer exists in your church directory.

JobChip.cancelledLong.context: One of nine states an edit can be in on its way to the church directory. JobChip.cancelledShort.context: Chip form: cancelled by a person. *Short* must fit inside a chip a few characters wide.

JobChip.stalledLong.context: One of nine states an edit can be in on its way to the church directory. Search.typeChildsName.context: The lobby kiosk's idle prompt — the largest words on the screen. A parent reads it and starts typing on the Latin-only keyboard beneath. Chinese must say the name is the child's English name (英文名字), because the keyboard has no other script; Spanish need not, since a Spanish speaker types a Latin name anyway. Addresses the parent as usted / 您. Spanish takes a noun phrase (Nombre de su hijo o hija), per the glossary's terseness rules: the imperative ran to two lines at the prompt's size.

Register.placeholderYourLast.context: The adult's surname, on the kiosk. English-only (英文): the kiosk keyboard has no IME.

Register.labelFirstName.context: The registration wizard's question list, on the kiosk: the row label beside the answer, for a child and for the adult alike. The kiosk keyboard is a fixed QWERTY with no IME, so the only name that can be typed here is an English one — say so (英文).

Register.labelLastName.context: As Register.labelFirstName — the surname row of the kiosk's question list. English-only for the same reason, so say so (英文).

Printer.setByPolicy.context: Reference note on the lobby kiosk’s printer screen, shown only when the printer was granted to Tally by the tablet’s own device-management policy rather than connected by hand. It exists to stop a volunteer hunting for a set-up step that does not exist. “This tablet’s own settings” means the managed configuration an administrator put on the device, not anything inside Tally.

Printer.tabletPolicy.context: Label on a folded section at the bottom of the lobby kiosk’s printer screen, seen only by staff. Behind it is the one Chrome setting an administrator must put on a managed tablet so the kiosk can reach the label printer. “Tablet” is the physical device the kiosk runs on.

Printer.tabletPolicyHint.source: This tablet is managed, so Chrome can be handed the printer once and for good. Paste the line below into the Chrome settings list in the tablet's management app.
Printer.tabletPolicyHint.context: One line of instruction inside that folded section, addressed to whoever is setting up a managed tablet while standing at it. “Managed” means an administrator controls the device through a management app; “the line below” is the Chrome policy value shown underneath, which is copied and pasted rather than typed.

Printer.tabletPolicyMore.source: The rest of the tablet settings, and what each one is for, are at {url}.
Printer.tabletPolicyMore.context: A quieter line under the copy button, pointing at Tally’s own page listing every other tablet setting. {url} is a web address and must be left exactly as it is.

Printer.policyCheck.source: Forget this printer and ask the tablet
Printer.policyCheck.context: Button on the lobby kiosk’s printer screen, inside a folded, staff-only block about the tablet’s device-management settings. Pressing it deletes the printer this kiosk has saved and then asks the tablet whether its own management policy hands one over — a way of testing whether that policy is working. “The tablet” is the Android device the kiosk runs on.

Printer.policyCheckHint.source: Checks whether the setting above is actually in force. Revoke this site's USB permission in Chrome first — Settings, then Site settings, then USB devices — or the printer comes back on that old permission and this proves nothing.
Printer.policyCheckHint.context: Warning above the button, on the lobby kiosk’s printer screen, in a folded staff-only block. It says the check only means something if Chrome’s own saved USB permission for this site is removed first, because otherwise the printer returns on that old permission and the result looks like a pass. “Settings, then Site settings, then USB devices” is a path through Chrome’s own menus and should use whatever those menus are called in this language.

Printer.policyCheckBusy.context: The same button’s label while the check is running, a second or two at most. Replaces the button’s usual words in place.

Printer.policyCheckFound.source: The tablet handed the printer over. The setting above is in force.
Printer.policyCheckFound.context: Result line under that button: the tablet’s management policy did hand a printer over, so the setting shown just above in the same block is working. Good news, stated plainly.

Printer.policyCheckNone.source: Nothing came from the tablet's settings. Either they are not in force or the printer is not plugged in — chrome://policy on this tablet says which.
Printer.policyCheckNone.context: Result line under that button: no printer arrived from the tablet’s settings. Deliberately does not conclude which of the two causes it was. “chrome://policy” is a literal address typed into the tablet’s browser and is never translated.

Printer.policyCheckFailed.source: The check could not be run, so nothing here was established either way. chrome://policy on this tablet is the answer.
Printer.policyCheckFailed.context: Result line under that button when the check itself could not run, which is different from the check coming back empty: nothing was learned in either direction. “chrome://policy” is a literal address typed into the tablet’s browser and is never translated.

Printer.policyCopied.context: Announced to screen readers when the Chrome printer setting has been copied to the clipboard. Not shown on screen.
